Prevention: Proper management of natural enemies through disciplined application of chemicals.
Minimize the use of broad-spectrum pesticides such as
Pyrethroids; although they kill pests, they also exterminate natural enemy species
Manage attendant ants by applying a ring of used engine oil around the stem, because these keep off many predators and parasites from accessing the aphids
Avoid applying more nitrogen than necessary because high levels of nitrogen fertilizer favour aphid reproduction.
Consult your extension worker on acceptable nitrogen rates
Monitoring: Monitor for aphids on young trees and take action when you observe 25% or more of leaf flushes infested with aphids
Take close observation of presence of ants.
Large numbers of ants climbing tree trunks indicate presence of aphids or other honeydew-producing insects.
Aphids prefer the underside of leaves; turn leaves over when checking for aphids
Check for evidence of natural enemies such as ladybeetles, lacewings, syrphid fly larvae, and the mummified skins of parasitized aphids
Direct Control: Spray ants with water-liquid soap solution at 1ml/L of water and sprays should be directed at the underside of the leaf
Spray affected plants with non- conventional plant protection products such as neem extracts
Restrictions: Consult your extension worker and always read the label for direction on use
Always wear protective gear (overalls, gumboots, goggles, caps, gloves and face masks) when handling chemicals
Under severe infestation, products like lambda cyhalothrin can be used to bring aphid population below damaging levels.
